title: Otis the Otter and the Wandering Notes
markdown:
Once, in a ferny valley, lived an otter named Otis, pebble-bright of eye, forever spotting little wonders. The charm sometimes landed him in a pickle. His job was Page-Turner for the Woodland Symphony Orchestra.

The Grand Concert was near. During rehearsal of the Whispering Willows Waltz, Mr. Quill — a badger conductor famed for fussiness — rapped his baton. Hedgehogs, squirrels, and mice stood ready in their smartest. It was Otis's turn to turn the page.

Then — a beetle. Rainbow-shelled, antennae twitching as if it had come to conduct. Otis leaned in, whiskers aquiver. The notes blurred.

Chaos: squeaks, thumps, and a monumental sigh from Mr. Quill. "Otis! That was the River Rondo, and you were admiring a beetle!"

Otis's ears drooped. "But it was very shiny."

Mr. Quill polished his spectacles. "The River Rondo needs focus, not sparkly insects."

The next day, nervous energy buzzed. "The River Rondo, from measure thirty-two!"

Music swelled like a bubbling stream. Otis tried to watch the notes. A plump mayfly, a show-off, looped dizzy circles before his nose. His quick eyes followed every twirl. The cue sailed past. The music faltered. Mei, a graceful heron, offered a soft questioning "Mmm."

A hot prickly feeling bloomed behind Otis's eyes. A pebble-weight settled in his chest. He did not need anyone to name it.

That evening he sat glum by the stream. Mei landed beside him. "You seem troubled."

"I can't focus. So many wonderful things. Mr. Quill thinks I'm hopeless."

Mei tilted her head. "You see those wonderful things. Your eyes are sharp. Perhaps it is about when to notice, and what to do with what you notice."

A tiny spark. Channeling, not shutting.

The Grand Concert arrived. The clearing hummed. Fireflies hung like fallen stars. Mr. Quill, surprisingly spry, raised his baton. The River Rondo approached. Otis took a breath. He was ready.

Then a mischievous gust. Leaves rustled, damp in the air. Papers fluttered. The River Rondo sheet cartwheeled up and snagged on a high oak branch. A gasp went through the audience. Otis's heart drummed like a frantic woodpecker. Mr. Quill went a delightful pink. The music sputtered out.

Otis remembered Mei. When you notice, and what you do. His quick eyes found the page in the oak.

"I see it!" Clear as a bell. He dove into the stream, rode the current to the oak's base, scrambled the rough bark, claws finding purchase. Mei called directions from below, steady as river stones. He plucked the page from the twig, whooped, and slid down into a splash.

He scrambled to the podium, damp page in paw. The orchestra stared, hopeful. Mr. Quill's baton hovered.

"Measure thirty-two," Otis announced, steady, and set the rescued page on the stand.

Mr. Quill nodded — a surprised, almost reverent bow — and raised the baton. The River Rondo began again, sweet and strong. Otis turned on time. He noticed the music now: the rhythm, the melody, the place the beetle was not invited.

Thunderous applause. The forest cheered. Otis had not become a different otter. He had given his noticing a job. He still saw wonderful things. He simply knew, sometimes, that the most wonderful thing on the stand was the next bar.

Afterward he found a mayfly resting on a fern, showing off to nobody, and he let it. The encore, he thought with a happy wiggle, could wait until the music was finished noticing him back.
